summary: This deck presents a 2023 case study on applying the frugal engineering process to socially conscious design for homeless individuals. It defines social and frugal innovation, emphasizes the 4 A's framework, and describes the design, specifications, and evaluation of a low-cost wearable jacket that transforms into a tent for weather protection and shelter. The prototype is assessed against commercial alternatives, showing favorable price and satisfactory performance, with limitations in thermal insulation and tent robustness.

content: Frugal Engineering Process for Frugal Innovation: Socially Conscious Designs for Homeless Individuals (Case study)

Social innovations are defined as new solutions (products, services, models, markets, processes, etc.) that simultaneously meet a social need (more effectively than existing solutions) and lead to new or improved capabilities and relationships and better use of assets and resources.
Frugal innovation is becoming a mainstream approach to many successful social innovations necessary for improving the affordability and accessibility of socially conscious product design solutions.
Frugal engineering needs to deliver on the 4 A’s – ‘acceptability, availability, accessibility, and affordability’ for successful product development
Understanding Frugal Engineering Process for Frugal Innovations: Socially Conscious Designs for Homeless Individuals, A Case Study, 2023
Case study: Design approach, Methods, and Validation
Problem Statement
Homelessness is defined as the state of being without a home.
Rising urbanization and socio-economic inequalities have increased homelessness worldwide.
Lack of shelter leads to poor physical health, mental stress, food insecurity, and financial hardship.
Berkeley, California:
44% of the counted homeless population slept outdoors, on streets, parks, or in tents.
49% of surveyed homeless individuals reported sleeping outdoors.
Los Angeles:
64% of homeless individuals had lived in the county for 10 years or more before becoming homeless.
Target: Design an innovative wearable prototype of a jacket (for weather protection) that can be transformed into a tent (for sleep/shelter)
Design criteria
Design methods
Transformable wearable prototype from jacket configuration to the tent configuration
Details of folds for jacket prototype (dimensions in mm)
Specifications of design
Comparison of tent configuration and jacket configuration is made with two separate products as no commercial transformable product exists for comparison
Evaluation of prototype
Overall, the factors considered, on average, both the tent and wearable jacket configurations were rated close to 1 (1.18 for the tent configuration and 0.91 for the wearable jacket state)
Price point for this frugally engineered prototype was lower than both the comparative commercial products.
The performance of this prototype was considered satisfactory within the set boundary conditions and design criteria for a socially conscious product.
Key drawbacks of the prototype mainly related to the thermal insulation and robustness of tent configuration
